subject: Post-call: Architecture & Networking alignment for NovaPay onboarding
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novapay.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@novapay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Architecture & Networking alignment for NovaPay onboarding

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on the integration: short summary, assumptions, and owners below.

Goal: Production-grade payments fraud scoring + decisioning via Redwood (low-latency scoring in-region, embeddings-backed reranking for candidate rules).

Key technical items we covered (and what we recommend):
- SDK & auth: start with Redwood SDK (Java/Node) + API key for initial dev; for Private deployment we recommend mTLS + customer-managed KMS. Laura will own the SDK onboarding checklist.
- Routing & fallbacks: primary route to a Dedicated model pool in us-west; configure routing policies to fallback to a smaller-cost model on overload. We'll share suggested policy JSON.
- Structured output / tool calling: use the function-calling schema for deterministic rule outputs (JSON schema attached sample). This enables deterministic rule invocation and auditability.
- Embeddings & rerank: generate 1536-d embeddings for historical events; use Redwood Rerank flow (embed -> vector store -> rerank) for candidate prioritization. We'll propose a batching cadence to minimize token costs.
- Networking / private connectivity: two options depending on privacy needs:
  1) Hosted + allowlist: Hosted API with IP allowlist + private DNS mapping (simpler).
  2) Private (VPC endpoint): VPC endpoint + egress via customer NAT, plus optional mutual TLS between customer gateway and Redwood edge.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Laura: SDK quickstart + sample function schema (attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf) — ETA 2026-12-03
- Marcus: specific egress IP ranges, TLS rotation plan, and sample VPC endpoint CFT — ETA 2026-12-01
- Alex/Priya: confirm preferred connectivity approach (Hosted allowlist vs Private VPC) and security contacts for SOC2 evidence — ETA 2026-12-02

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (sample code and function schema), nova-pay-ma-plan.xlsx (mutual action plan).

If helpful we can schedule a 60-min technical workshop (Marcus + Laura + NovaPay infra/security) this week. Proposed time slots: Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Thanks — Jasmine Liu

jasmine@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our infra/security side: 

1) Egress IPs: can you share the canonical list of outbound IPs we would need to allow? We need these for our firewall and to open firewall rules to the Redwood Hosted endpoints while we evaluate Private. The list in the call was pretty broad.

2) mTLS: for Private, will Redwood terminate the TLS at your edge and then establish mTLS to the customer gateway, or do we present a client cert from our side to your endpoint? We need to understand cert rotation and who holds the certs.

3) Embeddings size: you mentioned 1536-d — can you confirm the memory/per-query cost implications and any recommended quantization if we store full history?

We like the idea of a technical workshop. Tue (PST afternoon) works for our infra leads.

Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Architecture & Networking alignment for NovaPay onboarding

Alex — quick answers and a couple of concrete artifacts attached. Please see inline.

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 9:04 AM Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novapay.com> wrote:
> 1) Egress IPs: can you share the canonical list of outbound IPs we would need to allow?

We publish a stable egress block for Hosted endpoints and a separate set for Dedicated/Private edge nodes. Attached "private-connectivity-ip-ranges.csv" has the current CIDR list for our edge pool (note: subject to quarterly updates; we'll notify you). For Hosted allowlist: consider whitelisting the aggregate 52.43.120.0/22 and 18.205.0.0/16 (samples) and then tighten to the file once validated with your infra.

> 2) mTLS: for Private, will Redwood terminate the TLS at your edge and then establish mTLS to the customer gateway, or do we present a client cert from our side to your endpoint?

For Private (VPC endpoint) we support mutual TLS where the customer presents a client cert to the Redwood endpoint (mutual auth). Redwood also supports a model where Redwood presents a server cert and customer validates it (standard TLS) while we authenticate requests with per-team API keys; for stricter compliance you can elect mTLS where certs are rotated via your KMS/HSM and the Redwood control plane validates the client cert chain. We'll provide a cert-rotation playbook (attached).

> 3) Embeddings size: you mentioned 1536-d — can you confirm memory/per-query cost implications and any recommended quantization if we store full history?

1536-d embeddings using our default float32 encoding are ~6KB per vector. If you store 10M vectors that implies ~60GB raw; using 8-bit quantization (our recommended starting point) reduces storage ~4x with <2% quality loss for retrieval tasks. For reranking we suggest computing sparse candidate sets (top-K via approximate NN) then reranking with a denser scoring model to keep compute costs bounded. We can share an estimated cost sheet once you give expected QPS and history window.

Artifacts attached: private-connectivity-ip-ranges.csv, cert-rotation-playbook.pdf.

Action: I can present a draft VPC endpoint CloudFormation for your infra team in the workshop. Laura will cover SDK and function-calling schema.

- Marcus Lin
Lead Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
